title: Effects of coherent and incoherent measurement imperfections on multipartite quantum nonlocality and quantum key distribution
summary: Multipartite Bell nonlocality is a central resource for device-independent quantum information protocols, but its practical certification is inevitably affected by imperfect measurements. We analyze how coherent angular misalignment and incoherent outcome flipping affect Bell-value degradation and nonlocality thresholds in $n$-partite GHZ states based on the Mermin, Svetlichny, and Mermin--Ardehali--Belinskii--Klyshko (MABK) inequalities.
